title: Indiana Fever Dismiss GM Amber Cox Following President’s Sudden Exit, ESPN Reports
body:
The Indiana Fever announced a sweeping front‑office overhaul on Friday, dismissing General Manager Amber Cox just hours after President Kelly Krauskopf tendered her resignation. The rapid succession of exits signals a decisive shift in the franchise’s leadership as the team seeks to chart a new direction following a disappointing 2023‑24 season that left the club well outside the WNBA playoff picture.

Cox’s termination came amid a flurry of activity at the Fever’s Indianapolis headquarters. According to sources familiar with the situation, the decision was made by the ownership group, which has been under pressure to address the organization’s on‑court performance and off‑court business strategy. Cox, who was hired in 2022, oversaw a roster rebuild that included the high‑profile trade for former All‑Star Candace Parker and the signing of veteran guard Kelsey Plum. Despite those moves, the Fever finished the season with a 14‑26 record, missing the postseason for the second consecutive year. Insiders say the front office’s inability to translate talent acquisition into a cohesive, competitive unit was a primary factor in the board’s choice to start fresh.

President Kelly Krauskopf, who had served as the Fever’s top executive since 2020, also stepped down, citing personal reasons and a desire to pursue other opportunities within the sport. Krauskopf’s tenure was marked by efforts to modernize the franchise’s brand, increase community engagement, and secure new sponsorship deals. While she succeeded in elevating the Fever’s profile in the Indianapolis market, the team’s lackluster results on the court ultimately outweighed those achievements in the eyes of ownership. Her departure, coupled with Cox’s firing, leaves a significant leadership vacuum that the organization must fill quickly to maintain momentum on both the business and basketball sides.

Amid the turmoil, head coach Stephanie White appears set to retain her position, according to sources close to the franchise. White, who guided the Fever to a playoff berth in 2022 before the team regressed, will now shoulder the additional burden of stabilizing a roster that has been through multiple roster changes and coaching adjustments. Analysts suggest that White’s continued presence could provide a measure of continuity for players, but they also note that the coach will likely need greater support from a new GM to execute a clear long‑term vision. The Fever’s scouting department, player development staff, and analytics team are expected to undergo a review as the front office rebuild progresses.

The timing of the firings underscores the urgency felt by the Fever’s ownership to address systemic issues before the WNBA draft and free‑agency period. With the 2024 draft approaching, the franchise will be looking to appoint a general manager capable of balancing immediate roster upgrades with sustainable talent pipelines. Potential candidates include seasoned executives from other WNBA clubs, as well as rising executives from the NBA’s development ranks who have demonstrated an ability to navigate salary‑cap constraints while fostering competitive rosters. The new GM will also need to collaborate closely with White to align coaching philosophy with personnel decisions—a synergy that has eluded the Fever in recent years.

Looking ahead, the Fever’s next moves will be closely watched by fans and league observers alike. The dual departures create both a challenge and an opportunity: a fresh leadership team could revitalize a franchise that has struggled to regain its former prominence after a string of losing seasons. However, the pressure to deliver results quickly will be intense, especially as rival teams in the Eastern Conference continue to strengthen. The coming weeks will reveal whether Indianapolis can assemble a cohesive front office capable of translating strategic hires and roster tweaks into a winning culture, setting the stage for a possible return to the playoffs in the 2025 season.
